findings.title: Global canManage() also passes for a view-only groups permission
findings.body: `canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. An admin who has only an all-groups `view` permission therefore passes `requireManage()`. That check guards creating top-level groups, so a view-only grant lets the admin write groups. `canManage(GroupModel)` beside it correctly checks only `MANAGE`. Fix: check only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` here.

findings.title: canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, so a view-only all-groups permission lets the admin manage groups.
findings.body: `canManage()` passes `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` to `hasPermission`. The method returns true if any listed scope is granted. An admin who was given only `view` on all groups therefore passes `requireManage()` and can do anything gated on it, such as creating top-level groups. This looks like a copy of the `canView()` line. Check only `MANAGE` here.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body:
Group resources are named after the group ID: `resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()`, and that becomes the resource name. This loop instead passes `groupResource.getId()` (the internal resource ID) to `hasPermission`. There `findByName` never matches, so every check falls back to the all-groups resource. The loop then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result, and that set is stored as `UserModel.GROUPS` and used as group IDs to filter user search and count queries. `findByType` also returns the "Groups" type resource itself, so its ID ends up in the set too.

The result: an admin with VIEW_MEMBERS on a group gets a filter made of IDs that are not group IDs. User counts and search results are then wrong (usually empty), or wrongly granted through the all-groups fallback. Fix: use `groupResource.getName()` for both the check and the result, and skip the resource-type resource.

findings.title: requireManageMembers docstring names the wrong method.
findings.body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. It is the counterpart of `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, so the doc names the wrong check; it looks copied from `requireManageMembership`.
